cda1a0b82a66.text: AeroSense is a compact reader that combines four replaceable 100 µL wells, frequency-tagged blue LEDs, a filtered photodiode, ESP32 acquisition and a local phone interface. The eight-part enclosure fixes the optical geometry and separates sample gas from electronics cooling. Optical and airflow simulations guided filter selection and the inlet shelf, while assembly feedback informed the manual. Fluorescein measurements resolve four frequency channels and quantify cross-well responses. Explicit I/Q matrix correction distinguishes isolated controls, but transfer to simultaneous multi-well loading remains inconsistent; concentration recovery therefore requires further matched-control validation.

24c304b94e44.text: Optical and airflow models turn design choices into measurable targets. The reader separates four modulation channels, and isolated-source controls provide a measured mixing matrix. Applying that matrix explicitly exposes a gap between isolated and simultaneous loading: uniform 10 µM responses are only 48.3–69.4% of the sum predicted by the isolated controls. The matrix-derived estimates and residuals retain this discrepancy. A new concentration calibration needs matched single-source and mixed-source controls across concentrations under the same optical configuration.

Fluorescein measurements demonstrate four-frequency separation and quantify source mixing. The remaining loading-dependent discrepancy defines the next calibration experiment; reliable arbitrary-mixture concentration recovery has not yet been demonstrated.
